Food recommendations and, at the end, three simple ready-to-use itineraries for 6 days, 8 days, and 13 days depending on your time and budget. So, let's get started. Let's start with flights. From India, direct flights to Vietnam are mainly available to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. If you want to explore North Vietnam like Hanoi, Sapa, Ha Long Bay, and Ninh Binh, then land there. And if you want nightlife and modern city vibes, then Ho Chi Minh is the place for you to go. Round-trip tickets are generally available for 28,000 to 30,000. Depending on the season. Budget airlines like VietJet, Indigo, and AirAsia operate directly to Vietnam. To travel within Vietnam, you also need to take internal flights to cities like Phu Quoc and Da Nang. So, a combination of two or three cities can be a good plan. The Vietnam visa process is honestly very easy. You just need to apply for an e-visa online on the official government website. After the application, it takes around three to five working days and you get the visa via email in the form of a PDF file. The visa fee is approximately 25 to 30 USD, and this visa gives you 30 days of single entry. More than enough for a normal trip. A pro tip: whenever you are applying for the visa, keep your hotel booking and flight details handy because everything is asked in the form. While filling out the visa form, it is very important to select the entry port correctly. Otherwise, you might face some immigration issues. So, choose this very carefully. If you need any help with your visa form, DM us at Sands and Summits, and we will get your e-visa sorted within a week. Look, travel insurance is something people tend to ignore. But when a problem arises, you realize how important it was. In Vietnam, healthcare is expensive, especially for foreigners. So, always buy travel insurance. You can get a good plan for 10-15 days for under 800-1200 rupees. The currency of Vietnam is the Vietnamese Dong. 1 INR equals roughly 300 to 310 Dong. It keeps fluctuating a bit. My personal recommendation is to carry USD. You get better exchange rates. Plus, ATMs are very common in major cities. You can also withdraw cash using your card there. Just check the charges with your bank. Card payments aren't accepted everywhere. Especially in small cafes, local markets, or cabs. So, always keep some cash on hand. Data connectivity in Vietnam is quite solid. You can buy a Viettel, MobiFone, or VinaPhone SIM at the airport itself. Usually, a 7 to 10- day unlimited data plan is available for under 800 rupees. I personally prefer getting a SIM from the airport itself. Because those guys also help with instant SIM activation. In Vietnam , you will find stays for every budget. For backpackers, hostels start from 700 to 1000 per night. Mid-range hotels cost around 2500 to 4000 per night, and for premium resorts or riverside villas , it can go up to 7000 to 10000. If you are a couple or family, staying in central areas is the best option. Like the Old Quarter in Hanoi, beach-front resorts near My Khe Beach in Da Nang, or District 1 in Ho Chi Minh City. The benefit of staying in prime areas is that everything is within walking distance, and it feels quite safe in the evenings. We at Sands and Summits have 50+ contracted rates for hotels all across Vietnam. So, DM us before booking your next Vietnam trip. For transport, options in Vietnam are very convenient. For short distances, you can use Grab. Renting a scooter is also quite popular. You can get a scooter for 500 to 700 rupees. Just ensure you have an international driving license if you are riding yourself. To travel between cities, there are many options like buses and trains. But my preference is to book a domestic flight within the country. Vietnam's transport system is very well connected. So, even first-time travelers can manage it easily. Grab, for both local cabs and food delivery; Gojek, for bike taxis and cheap transfers; Google Translate, especially for menus and directions; Currency Converter, to check the live exchange rate for that particular day; Maps.me, this is an offline version of maps and it's useful especially if you are going to rural areas like Sapa or Ha Giang. English is understood at a basic level in Vietnam, but there might be a language barrier in local markets and remote towns. So, do keep the Google Translate app, especially by downloading the Vietnamese to English option to use it offline. The locals are very polite and helpful. Just smile and talk. Everything is manageable. Now , talking about food, the street food here is literally next level. Some of the must-tries are Pho. This is the Vietnamese noodle soup. Banh mi. This is a Vietnamese baguette sandwich. Spring rolls. And for coffee lovers, there are various options. Vegetarian travelers can also find plenty of options. Just ask for "Chay". So, the basics are covered now. Flights, visa, insurance, money, stay, transport— everything is clear. Now let’s talk about the most exciting part. The itinerary: which cities to visit in Vietnam, and how much can be covered in how many days? Whether you have 6 days, 9 days, or 13 days, there can be a perfect plan for every situation. Let’s get into that next. So, we went to Vietnam for eight days. And trust me , these eight days literally just flew by. We covered Hanoi, Da Nang, and Ho Chi Minh City, and honestly, every city had its own vibe. From calm lakes to crazy nightlife, everything was insane. Our plan looked like this. Day one, we landed in Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam, and headed straight to the Old Quarter. There is a unique energy amidst the narrow lanes, French architecture, and constant honking here . After checking in and a little rest, we headed out in the evening to explore Hanoi city. We started with Hoan Kiem Lake, which is right in the heart of the city. Then we visited the Temple of Literature, and in the evening, we went for the water puppet show, which is something very unique in Vietnam. At night, while roaming the Old Quarter Night Market and Beer Street, we tried local street food like Banh mi, Pho, and coffee. Everything is completely authentic in Hanoi. And yes, the famous Hanoi Train Street. Where a real train literally passes at a distance of one foot from you. This is an absolute must . The moment when the train passes by is pure adrenaline. The next day we left for Ninh Binh, which people often call Ha Long Bay on land. This is about a two-hour drive from Hanoi and the whole route was so scenic with green rice fields, limestone mountains, and countryside views. We started with Hoa Lu, the ancient capital of Vietnam. There are old temples and royal palaces here where Vietnam's early history began. Then came the Trang An boat ride . This is the absolute highlight. Imagine sitting in a small boat and passing over a crystal-clear river. With limestone cliffs and caves on both sides, it feels unreal. Lastly, we trekked up to the Mua Cave viewpoint. There are around 500 stairs, but the panoramic view from the top, amidst rice fields and mountains, is 100%worth the climb. By evening, we returned to Hanoi. Day three was all about luxury and pure fun. We left for Ha Long Bay, one of the most beautiful places in Vietnam, and boarded our five-star overnight cruise, and this was something else. During the day, we went kayaking through limestone caves. At sunset, there was a full party and live music on the rooftop deck, and at night , dancing under the stars. The cruise, the food, the people; the entire experience was totally luxurious. The next morning after breakfast, we checked out of the cruise and headed straight to the airport to catch our evening flight to Da Nang. By evening, we arrived and checked in near My Khe Beach. One of the cleanest and most beautiful beaches in Vietnam. Day five. Today was one of the most awaited days: Ba Na Hills. We left early in the morning and took the cable car. Fun fact: this is one of the longest cable cars in the world. As soon as we reached the top, it felt like we had arrived in a European mountain village. We saw the famous Golden Hand Bridge. Those same giant hands that you see everywhere on Instagram. Then we explored the French Village, the wine cellar, and the alpine roller coaster. Yes, a roller coaster in the hills. You will need an entire day just to explore and soak in the beauty of Ba Na Hills. Day six: we explored Da Nang. We started with Son Tra Peninsula, also called Monkey Mountain, for panoramic views of the city and the beautiful Lady Buddha statue overlooking the sea. Then we headed to the Marble Mountains. You take an elevator to the top, and inside, the ancient caves, temples, pagodas, and ruins give the whole area a mystical feel. Then we went to Coconut Village, where we did a basket boat ride. You literally ride in a round bamboo boat while spinning around . The locals show you their entire fishing style and tricks. A super fun and very unique experience. In the evening, we arrived at Hoi An Ancient Town. Asia’s most romantic and picturesque town. Narrow lantern-lit streets, riverside cafes, Japanese Bridge, and that peaceful vibe. Everything in this city is so dreamy. In the evening, we took a river boat ride and released our lanterns into the river with a wish. Next day, we checked out from Da Nang and took a flight to Ho Chi Minh City. After checking in and some rest, we explored some of the city's iconic spots like Notre Dame Cathedral, Saigon Post Office, and Ben Thanh Night Market. As evening fell, we went to Bui Vien Walking Street, and the nightlife here is absolutely wild. Imagine an entire street full of pubs, neon lights, live music, and people dancing everywhere. It’s literally a never-ending party. If you love nightlife, this place is a must. Day eight. Today we set out for the Cu Chi Tunnels. Around 60-70 km away from Ho Chi Minh City. These tunnels were built during the Vietnam War. Where soldiers lived, fought, and even built underground hospitals. The entire system is around 250 km long. Here, you actually get to go inside the tunnels yourself. It is definitely a bit claustrophobic, but it is rich in history. After the tour, we returned to our hotel, quickly checked out, and headed for our evening flight back to India. And just like that, our eight-day Vietnam journey ended. So, this was the story of our eight-day trip. But obviously, not everyone has eight days. Some people go on short leaves. Some people plan long holidays. So, if you are planning a Vietnam trip, this simple breakdown will be useful for you. If you have got six days, then it is best to cover Hanoi and Da Nang. North Vietnam's culture and city life, Ha Long Bay's luxury, and Da Nang's beaches and Ba Na Hills 'adventure make for a balanced short trip. If you have got 10 days, then you can do Hanoi, Da Nang, and Phu Quoc Island. Phu Quoc is a hidden paradise. Crystal clear beaches, luxury resorts, and lots of water activities. In this, you get the perfect combo of mountains, culture, and beaches. And if you have got 13 days, then go all in on Hanoi, Da Nang, Phu Quoc, and Ho Chi Minh City— meaning the entire Vietnam from North to South. A complete experience, from the cultural capital to beach luxury and crazy nightlife. These three itineraries are currently presented on your screen.
